title: Amount of substance bridges entities and laboratory matter
question: How does amount of substance connect an entity count to molar mass, ideal-gas volume, and electric charge?
answerPreview: Amount of substance n uses the exact Avogadro constant to relate entities and moles; molar mass, an explicitly chosen ideal-gas state, and charge number then determine dependent mass, volume, and Faraday conversions.
summary: Scale a declared elementary entity from count to amount, mass, an assumption-bound ideal-gas volume, and Faraday charge without treating dependent conversions as independent predictions.

observationStage.title: Exact definitions and a declared pressure convention
observationStage.question: Which International System of Units (SI) values are exact, and which state variables must be stated before an ideal-gas volume is meaningful?

items.label: Avogadro constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly. One mole contains exactly this many specified elementary entities.

items.label: Elementary charge
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly. Multiplying it by the Avogadro constant gives the exact Faraday constant.

items.label: Standard atmosphere
items.explanation: The non-SI standard atmosphere is exactly 101325 pascals. It is one declared pressure convention, not a universal unstated standard state.

observationStage.conclusion: The Avogadro constant and elementary charge are exact SI defining values, and the standard atmosphere is an exact pressure conversion. An ideal-gas volume still requires both temperature and pressure to be stated.

guidedBlocks.title: Amount of substance counts specified entities in moles
body: Amount of substance n is a physical quantity whose SI unit is the mole. The elementary entity must be specified: atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, or another defined group are not interchangeable counts.
The exact relation is N = n N_A, where N is the number of specified entities and N_A is the Avogadro constant.
One mole therefore corresponds to exactly 6.022 140 76 x 10^23 specified elementary entities.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; IUPAC Green Book, 3rd edition, 2nd printing
caveats: Entity count is dimensionless, while amount of substance is a distinct quantity with SI unit mol.

guidedBlocks.title: Mass scaling needs a molar mass
body: For a specified substance or entity, mass follows m = n M, where M is its molar mass.
Changing amount scales mass linearly only while composition and molar mass remain fixed.
Molar mass is an input property or measured reference for the selected substance; it is not determined by the Avogadro constant alone.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: IUPAC Green Book, 3rd edition, 2nd printing; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: IUPAC section 2.10, amount and molar quantities; BIPM section 5.4.8
caveats: Mixtures, isotopic composition, chemical association, and sample impurities require an appropriately defined molar mass.

guidedBlocks.title: Ideal-gas volume depends on a stated state
body: Under the ideal-gas assumptions, p V = n R T and therefore V = n R T divided by p.
The standard-ideal-gas preset declares 273.15 K and one standard atmosphere, exactly 101325 Pa. Another common reference uses 273.15 K and 100000 Pa, so the two dependent molar volumes differ.
Neither pressure-temperature pair is an unstated universal standard state. Always carry the selected state convention with the volume.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: IUPAC Green Book, 3rd edition, 2nd printing; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: IUPAC sections 2.11 and 4.3; BIPM non-SI pressure-unit table
caveats: Real gases can require an equation of state with composition-dependent non-ideal corrections.

guidedBlocks.title: The Faraday constant scales elementary charge to a mole
body: The Faraday constant is F = N_A e. Because N_A and the elementary charge e have exact fixed SI values, F is exact in the current SI.
If each specified entity transfers signed charge number z in elementary-charge units, the dependent charge is Q = z n F.
This relation converts a declared amount and charge number. It does not predict whether a chemical reaction occurs, reaches completion, or transfers that charge with perfect efficiency.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: BIPM defining constants; CODATA Faraday constant entry
caveats: Electrochemical yield, side reactions, and current efficiency are outside this conversion.

technicalBlocks.title: The current mole definition no longer fixes carbon-12 molar mass exactly
body: Before 20 May 2019, the mole definition referred to the number of atoms in 0.012 kilogram of carbon-12. The current SI instead fixes the numerical value of N_A exactly.
Consequently, the molar mass of carbon-12 is no longer defined to be exactly 0.012 kg/mol. It is experimentally determined and remains extremely close to that value, with stated uncertainty.
The activity therefore treats molar mass as an explicit input and does not use 0.012 kg/mol as an exact current-SI identity.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: BIPM section 2.3.3 and note on molar mass of carbon-12; CODATA molar mass constant and carbon-12 entries
caveats: Rounded teaching values must not be relabeled as exact defining values.

technicalBlocks.title: Every displayed bulk value has an explicit dependency graph
body: Entity count depends on n and N_A. Mass additionally depends on selected molar mass M. Ideal-gas volume additionally depends on the chosen T, p, and the ideal-gas equation.
Faraday charge depends on n, signed charge number z, and F. These outputs share n and must not be treated as independent evidence for one another.
Changing a state convention changes only state-dependent outputs such as ideal-gas volume; it does not change entity count or mass.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; IUPAC Green Book, 3rd edition, 2nd printing
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Amount, molar quantity, ideal-gas, and charge relationships
caveats: A dependent conversion cannot serve as an independent prediction of its own input assumptions.

technicalBlocks.title: Large entity counts need an honest numerical representation
body: Macroscopic entity counts exceed the exact-integer range of ordinary binary floating-point numbers. The engine formats N in bounded scientific notation rather than claiming unit-by-unit integer precision.
The selected decimal amount is treated as the declared input quantity value. Its displayed particle count inherits that input precision even though N_A itself is exact.
All controls are bounded so mass, volume, charge, and logarithmic count remain finite.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; tour-content-2026-07-26
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Avogadro definition; particle-to-mole-scaler output and bounds contract
caveats: Exact defining constants do not remove rounding or uncertainty from user-supplied amounts and molar masses.

equationSteps.label: Entity count from amount of substance
equationSteps.explanation: The specified entity count N is the amount n multiplied by the exact Avogadro constant.
caveats: The identity requires the elementary entity to be specified.

equationSteps.label: Mass from molar mass
equationSteps.explanation: For fixed composition, sample mass is amount of substance multiplied by the declared molar mass.
caveats: Molar mass is an explicit input and may carry uncertainty.

equationSteps.label: Ideal-gas volume at a declared state
equationSteps.explanation: This dependent volume follows only under the ideal-gas model at the selected temperature and pressure convention.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: IUPAC Green Book, 3rd edition, 2nd printing; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update
equationSteps.sourceLocator: IUPAC ideal-gas and standard-pressure entries; BIPM pressure units
caveats: The equation omits non-ideal interactions and composition-dependent corrections.

equationSteps.label: Faraday charge conversion
equationSteps.expression: F = N_A e; Q = z n F
equationSteps.explanation: For a declared signed charge number z per entity, amount scales to charge through the exact Faraday constant.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
equationSteps.sourceLocator: SI defining constants; CODATA Faraday constant entry
caveats: The conversion does not model reaction completion or current efficiency.

checkpoints.prompt: If amount n doubles while molar mass M, temperature T, pressure p, and signed charge number z remain fixed, which displayed outputs double?

choices.label: Entity count, mass, ideal-gas volume, and Faraday charge
Only entity count and mass double
None of the dependent outputs double

checkpoints.explanation: Expected outcome: N = n N_A, m = n M, V = n R T/p, and Q = z n F are all linear in n when M, T, p, and z are held fixed, so all four outputs double. This ungraded checkpoint records no score.
